answer.evidence: radon/metrics.py:98-117 (mi_compute) holds the MI formula. Points to check: (1) The guard on line 104 only returns 100.0 for volume<=0 or sloc<=0, so math.log is safe, but this also hides cases where complexity or comments are odd. (2) Line 108 applies sqrt(2.46*radians(comments)), with comments as a percentage. A negative value would raise a ValueError in sqrt, so the input range of 0-100 needs validating. (3) Lines 110-116 follow the original 171 - 5.2 ln(V) - 0.23 G - 16.2 ln(LOC) + 50 sin(sqrt(2.4 * perCM)) form. The constant 2.46 differs from the usual 2.4 and should be justified. (4) Line 117 clamps nn_mi*100/171 to [0,100], which gives the bounded score. Add boundary tests for this. (5) mi_rank at line 157 uses boolean arithmetic for the thresholds, so check the 9 and 19 edges. Secondary review in radon/raw.py: confirm how sloc, comment lines and the comment percentage are produced, since those feed mi_parameters. Check the denominator and whether multiline strings are counted as comments.
